exercise.title: The augmented triad
exercise.why: An augmented triad is a major triad with the 5th raised a half step, so listening for that one note tells the two chords apart.

cells.text: Tap {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} on the staff below: C major, one note at a time.

Now tap {{1}} {{3}} {{#5}} on this staff: C augmented. Only the top note moved, up a half step to the ringed {{#5}}.
Go between the two staffs until you can hum the raised note before you tap it.

Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Go from C to Caug, then from Cm to Cdim: in the first pair the 5th goes up a half step, in the second it goes down.
Keep going until you can name all four with your eyes closed.
Press C, Caug and F below, in that order and in a slow, even count. The raised note of Caug sits a half step under a note of F, so it leads there.

Then press G, Gaug and C here in the same way.
When you change the key, the chords are new but the raised 5th still leads up a half step into the next chord.
